title: Enterprise activity: product selection
competency: Identify enterprise activities and the factors for selecting a product.

keywords.def: A group or individual activity that raises money, such as baking cakes, washing cars or making cards.
How often and how much customers need or want a product.
The profit gained compared with the money put into a business.

en.text: An enterprise activity raises money, as a group (baking cakes, washing cars) or individually (making cards). Choosing the right product is the building block of a business and must keep up with customers' changing needs. Key factors: the product most often needed (demand), enough funding, starter materials (source, quality, quantity), the best return on investment, and skilled staff who keep costs low by reducing waste.

screens.title: What sells near a school?
screens.ask: Near a school, which product will probably sell most often?
screens.after: Students need exercise books and pens every day: high frequency of demand.

screens.title: Enterprise and product selection
paras: An enterprise activity might be a group activity (baking cakes, washing cars) or an individual activity (making cards) that raises money.
Choosing the right product or service is the building block of every business; the product is the buyer's first contact.
Customers' needs change fast: note what customers ask for and the market trends.

screens.title: Factors for choosing a product
table: Is it needed often? (most frequent need = best chance)
Is there enough money for production, promotion and distribution?
Where from? What quality? How much?
Does it give the best profit for the money?
Are skilled people available? Can waste be reduced?

opts: By reducing wastage with skilled workers
screens.ans: By reducing wastage with skilled workers

screens.text: Two products: A sells 100 a week with 5 Birr profit each; B sells 10 a week with 20 Birr profit each. Which gives a better weekly return?
screens.why: A: 100 × 5 = 500 Birr; B: 10 × 20 = 200 Birr. Frequent demand can beat a high profit per item.
screens.clue: Multiply sales by profit per item.
